title: New Atlantic Council brief examines Bangladesh's changing aid landscape
excerpt: Published on 26 October 2026, the brief looks at how development assistance to Bangladesh is shifting and recommends front-loading concessional borrowing while it is still available.
content:
Research · Aid financing · Atlantic Council, 26 October 2026

At a glance

  • Title: Bangladesh’s changing development assistance landscape: Manifestations, implications, and opportunities
  • Authors: Leon S. Waskin, Jon F. Danilowicz and Imran Shauket
  • Publisher: Atlantic Council
  • Published: 26 October 2026
  • Geography: Bangladesh (a companion brief covers Pakistan)

Summary

The brief examines how development assistance to Bangladesh is changing, what that means for the country and where opportunities remain. Among its recommendations, the authors argue that Bangladesh should front-load concessional borrowing while that window is still open.

Why it matters

Falling grant aid, pressure on humanitarian budgets and Bangladesh’s move away from the most concessional terms all affect the funding available to NGOs and government programmes. The brief is a useful starting point for organisations planning their funding strategies for the next three to five years.
